title: Stack a zinc CR2032 coin cell with tweezers and dose its electrolyte by pipette
instruction: Assemble the zinc coin cell in the can that sits in the white mould, using the tweezers for every part: one zinc disc on the floor of the can, then the glass-fibre separator. Then use the pipette, set to 80 uL, to draw electrolyte from the tube and dispense all of it onto the separator (to the first stop; blowing out is optional). Then add the second zinc disc, the steel spacer, the wave spring and the cap, open side down. Every part must lie flat and centred in the can. Press the cap down with your other hand. Put the tweezers and the pipette back in their stands and let go.
context: Battery-materials labs test electrodes in CR2032 coin cells assembled by hand with tweezers. Hand assembly limits throughput and cell-to-cell reproducibility, which is why labs build coin-cell robots (AutoBASS, ODACell), and misaligned electrodes cost capacity and efficiency (NPL GPG 153; DGIST alignment study). Published aqueous-zinc recipe, built in air, ending where labs hand the cell to the crimper.
setup: Both arms empty, grippers open, at the station's ready pose. Each gripper finger pad wears a fresh single-use cover: 50 um polyethylene film wrapped over the pad and taped on its back, so electrolyte never reaches the robot. A white polyethylene-backed absorbent bench pad (400x300 mm) is taped to the table under the work. White POM mould 60x60x20 mm (20.3 mm pocket, 2 mm deep), taped down at x 0.32, y -0.06, holding an MTI CR2032 304SS can (20.0 mm OD, about 19.5 mm inside, 2.9 mm tall; measure and record), open side up. Bergeon 6460 plastic tweezers (119x15x11 mm; tips about 30 mm apart at rest; measure and record), tips down, legs opening along y, in a POM stand 40x40x30 mm with a 37x9 mm slot 25 mm deep, taped down at x 0.28, y 0.02. Two 90 mm glass petri dishes lined with weighing paper on 1 mm silicone, taped down; parts in a row along x, 25 mm apart. Dish A at x 0.32, y -0.17: zinc 12x0.10 mm (x 0.295), Whatman GF/A separator 19x0.26 mm (x 0.32), zinc (x 0.345). Dish B at x 0.22, y -0.13: MTI CR20SPA10 spacer 15.8x1.0 mm (x 0.195), MTI CR20WS-SPR wave spring (about 15 mm OD, 1.2 mm high; measure and record) (x 0.22), MTI CR2032 cap with fitted PP gasket (about 19.3 mm OD across the gasket, about 2 mm tall; measure and record), open side down (x 0.245). Ward's 10-100 uL micropipette set to 80 uL with a fresh 200 uL tip (hook to tip about 185 mm; measure and record), hung by its finger hook in a printed holder at x 0.40, y 0.10: 60x60x8 mm base, post at +x, the 22 mm cradle open towards the robot, set about 203 mm up so the tip hangs about 10 mm clear. 1.5 mL tube with 1.0 mL 2 M ZnSO4 in a POM rack 30x30x25 mm at x 0.24, y -0.22. Two phones on clamp arms inside a diffuse LED ring light: phone A 45 cm above the mould on its 3x camera (4K; a field about 21x12 cm, about 0.055 mm per pixel, the can about 360 px across) films the can; phone B, 60 cm up on its 1x camera, films the whole station. For scoring: a dial depth gauge (0.01 mm, 1.5 mm flat probe tip), a multimeter with a flat-tipped probe in a 50 g brass weight, and a 0.001 g scale. STL files for printed parts provided.
scoring: Procedure (reset notes): two overhead videos, fingertip-cover blot, depth gauge, meter, 0.001 g scale; R0 = max(5 Ohm, 1/5 of the lowest of 3 hand-built cells, read the same way). Video (phone A): order of arrival; offset = part centre to can axis, from the gaps to the wall, in its last frame with the arm away; zinc-to-zinc from those centres; finger travel = how far fingertip contacts move a part, summed over the trial. After the trial, in this order: blot; lift the cap and spring (if present) out onto a tared boat and weigh them; depth gauge on the spacer's top at 4 points 6.5 mm from the axis, 90 deg apart; meter from the spacer (weighted probe) to the can wall; weigh the can with its contents. Electrolyte = the two weighings minus the dry mass of exactly the parts present, each weighed alone before the trial. Flat: the 4 gauge heights within 0.3 mm of each other, none over the nominal 1.46 mm stack by more than 0.3 mm. 1.0: zinc, separator, electrolyte, zinc, spacer, spring, cap (open side down) in order, each once, moved only with tweezers; flat; zincs and zinc-to-zinc max 1.0 mm, spacer 1.5, spring under 2.25; 0.080-0.120 g; cap pressed, seated; over R0; tools stowed; fingers 3 cm from tools and cell for 1 s. 0.5: same, but zinc 1.0-2.0 mm, spacer 1.5-1.85, 0.050-0.079 or 0.121-0.150 g, a tool out or fingers not clear. 0.25: zinc, separator, electrolyte, zinc, spacer in order, flat, zinc max 2.0 mm, spacer under 1.85, 0.050-0.150 g, over R0; spring or cap missing, inverted, unseated or unpressed. Else 0, incl. wet blot, under R0, spring on the wall (2.25 mm or more), electrolyte off the separator, a part lifted back out, finger travel of 1.0 mm or more on any part (cap press exempt).
reset_notes: Score in this order (cap and spring need not be present): press each gripper's covered fingertips on blot paper (wet mark = 0), then peel the covers into zinc waste. Lift the cap and spring, if present, onto a tared boat with plastic tweezers; weigh. Can in the mould, depth gauge zeroed on the rim: read the spacer's top at 4 points 6.5 mm from the axis (0/90/180/270 deg). Stand the 50 g weighted probe on the spacer's centre, touch the other probe to the can's wall; read on 2 kOhm after 5 s. Lift the can by its wall and weigh it. Electrolyte = boat + can minus the dry mass of the parts present (each weighed alone, 0.001 g, before the trial). R0 cells are hand-built and read the same way. Then take the cell apart; can, cap, spacer and spring are reused: rinse in water then isopropanol, dry, replace if deformed. New each trial: two 12 mm zinc discs and a 19 mm GF/A separator (punched in batches of 20, kept flat), a pipette tip, pad covers. Refill the tube to 1.0 mL; wipe spills; dry the pad. The robot never touches the electrolyte: covers take any contact, the tweezers are plastic and rinsed, only the disposable tip meets the liquid. Wear nitrile gloves and eye protection (2 M ZnSO4 irritates). Collect used electrolyte, tips, separators, covers and wipes as zinc waste, never down the drain.
fidelity: 480 Hz. Zinc: rigid 0.1 mm discs. GF/A: rigid 0.26 mm disc (real one wets and clings). Linings, wave spring: soft contacts. Tweezers: rigid legs, sprung hinge. Can fixed in mould. Liquid is an event: let-up 2 mm under the surface loads 80 uL; a press 1-6 mm above the separator, within 3 mm of the axis, adds 0.105 g; else spills. Pad covers not modelled. Discs may sink into each other under the press, so the meter's order check uses the step before it. No crimp.
